description: Interpretive notes from one rehearsal are not consistently reaching absent players, and later rehearsals keep repeating the same fixes because the note trail is incomplete. All ensemble names are fictional.

user_profile.persona: 33-year-old rehearsal coordinator trying to stop repeated note loss between sessions
user_profile.context: The rehearsal process is sound, but information is not traveling cleanly from the room to the full ensemble roster
user_profile.communication_style: Detail-sensitive and efficient, wants notes grouped by piece and issue type

fact_sheet.fact: Elara Vance is the Rehearsal Coordinator for the Aethelred Symphony Orchestra; her email is e.vance@aethelredsymphony.org.
Maestro Julian Croft has been the Principal Conductor of the Aethelred Symphony Orchestra since 2018.
Concertmaster Anya Sharma is responsible for leading the first violin section and marking bowings for all string parts.
The Aethelred Symphony Orchestra has a full roster of 95 active musicians for the 2024-2025 season.
Principal Cellist Marcus Thorne provides sectional feedback on intonation and phrasing for the low strings.
Full orchestra rehearsals are scheduled every Tuesday and Thursday from 7:00 PM to 9:30 PM.
All full orchestra rehearsals take place in Lyra Hall, Room 3B, located at 1550 Cadence Avenue.
The last rehearsal where note loss was a significant issue was on Tuesday, November 12, 2024.
The next rehearsal is scheduled for Thursday, November 14, 2024, and will focus on Stravinsky's 'The Firebird Suite'.
The 'Winter Solstice Gala' concert is scheduled for December 21st, 2024, at the Grand Orpheum Theatre.
The program for the Winter Solstice Gala includes Mahler's Symphony No. 5, Stravinsky's 'The Firebird Suite (1919)', and Strauss's 'An Alpine Symphony'.
A note from the Nov. 12th rehearsal specified a change to a sforzando-piano (sfp) in the brass section in measure 211 of Mahler's Symphony No. 5, Movement I.
Maestro Croft requested the piccolo player to switch to the third flute for measures 88-104 of the 'Infernal Dance' section in Stravinsky's 'The Firebird Suite'.
The dynamic marking in the strings for the 'On the Summit' section of Strauss's 'An Alpine Symphony' (Rehearsal Mark 98) was changed from fortissimo (ff) to forte-piano (fp).
Second violinist Kenji Tanaka was absent from the November 12th rehearsal due to a family emergency.
Kenji Tanaka missed the note that all second violins must use an up-bow for the first note of measure 74 in Mahler's Symphony No. 5.
First horn Sofia Rossi was absent on November 7th and missed a note regarding articulation in 'The Firebird Suite'.
The note Sofia Rossi missed was to use a legato tongue instead of a slur for the solo passage at Rehearsal Mark 12 in 'The Firebird Suite'.
The up-bow correction for the second violins in Mahler's Symphony No. 5 (measure 74) had to be repeated three times during the November 12th rehearsal.
Elara Vance estimates that 25 minutes of rehearsal time were lost in October 2024 due to repeating corrections from previous sessions.
The current system for rehearsal notes is a single, spiral-bound Moleskine notebook (black, A5 size) kept on the conductor's podium.
During rehearsal, the notebook is passed to the relevant section leader to write down a note, then returned to Maestro Croft's podium.
After each rehearsal, Elara Vance is responsible for taking the notebook to her office (Room 12A, Lyra Hall) for safekeeping.
An internal audit on November 1st, 2024, showed that notes from the physical logbook fail to reach 80% of absent players before the next rehearsal.
The proposed digital solution is a cloud-based application called 'EnsembleFlow'.
EnsembleFlow allows notes to be tagged by piece, measure, and issue type (e.g., #dynamics, #articulation, #bowing).
The EnsembleFlow system is configured to automatically email a PDF summary of all new notes to the entire orchestra roster at 10:30 PM after every rehearsal.
The annual subscription for EnsembleFlow's 'Orchestra' plan is $750 for up to 100 users.
The trial account login for EnsembleFlow is available at https://app.ensembleflow.io/login with username 'aethelred_admin'.
Maestro Croft uses a 12.9-inch iPad Pro (Model A2461) with the ForScore app for his digital scores, which must be compatible with any new system.
